top_issues: Granite boulders have severe UV/texture artifacts (visible checkerboard faceting and contour-line stepping) and read as muddy brown clay rather than crisp light-grey speckled Sierra granite.
Pine trees are ultra-low-poly stacked cones with flat shading, zero needle alpha cards, and no bark texture, completely breaking photorealism.
Ground/trail dust is an oversaturated neon-orange smooth surface with visible polygon faceting and an artificial, ruler-straight pebble strip along the water edge.
Water lacks clarity and rocky streambed refraction; it looks like murky olive-brown gelatin rather than crystal-clear Sierra snowmelt over submerged stones.
Background sky/fog has a visible grid/checkerboard artifact and overly dense, milky orange haze that washes out depth.
`hero_low` camera is blocked by a massive, blurry, low-res foreground boulder covering 75% of the frame.
code_suggestions: In gen.py / ue_main.py: Fix granite boulder UVs and normals—enable smooth vertex normals, use triplanar/world-aligned projection in the granite material to eliminate checkerboard and contour-stepping artifacts, and generate a high-frequency salt-and-pepper noise texture for granite albedo/bump.

In gen.py: Replace the low-poly stacked-cone tree meshes with higher-detail conifer geometry (irregular branch tiers, vertex-displaced foliage clusters or alpha-tested needle cards, and textured dark-brown bark trunks).

In gen.py: Scatter dense multi-scale cobbles, angular granite rocks, and submerged pebbles across the creek bed and banks (like refs 4-6) to break up the smooth ditch geometry and hide the sharp shoreline seam.

In ue_main.py: Fix the camera transform for `hero_low` so it isn't intersecting/occluded by a foreground boulder, and switch water material to SingleLayerWater shading model with refraction/absorption so submerged rocks are clearly visible.
